subsystems.name: Prospecting and resource mapping
subsystems.role: prove where the ice is, how much there is and in what form before committing hardware.

subsystems.name: Excavation and hauling
subsystems.role: get icy regolith from the cold trap into the processing unit.

subsystems.name: Volatile extraction
subsystems.role: heat the icy soil so the water leaves it, then catch the vapour before it escapes.
parts: sealed processing chamber or sublimation tent

subsystems.name: Water processing and electrolysis
subsystems.role: turn dirty meltwater into clean water, oxygen and hydrogen.

subsystems.name: Surface power
subsystems.role: run heaters, drills and electrolysers through a two-week lunar night in permanent cold.
parts: solar arrays on tall masts at a sunlit ridge

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: keep electronics warm enough to work while keeping captured ice cold enough to stay frozen.

buildSteps.title: Prospect from orbit
buildSteps.detail: Neutron spectrometers and radar map hydrogen-rich ground; infrared spectrometers confirm it is water rather than hydroxyl. Remote sensing showed ice in permanently shadowed polar craters and, separately, trace water on sunlit surfaces.

buildSteps.title: Prospect from the surface
buildSteps.detail: A rover lands on a sunlit ridge, drives into the shadow, and drills or scoops samples into an oven. The released gases are weighed and analysed to give the ice concentration and depth — the number that decides whether mining is worth it.

buildSteps.title: Emplace the plant
buildSteps.detail: Equipment is landed near a permanently shadowed crater but powered from adjacent high ground that gets sunlight most of the time, since the cold traps themselves never see the sun.

buildSteps.title: Excavate
buildSteps.detail: A robotic bucket drum or auger breaks up the frozen regolith — which is as hard as concrete when ice-cemented — and moves it into a sealed hopper. Dust is abrasive and electrostatically sticky, so seals and bearings are the vulnerable parts.

buildSteps.title: Heat and capture volatiles
buildSteps.detail: The soil is heated, either in a sealed chamber or in place under a tent laid over the ground, so the ice sublimes directly to vapour. A cold trap held at around minus 200 °C freezes the vapour back out as clean ice, while other gases such as carbon monoxide and methane are separated off.

buildSteps.title: Purify the water
buildSteps.detail: The captured ice is melted and filtered to remove dust, then stored as ice or liquid, or fed straight to the electrolyser.

buildSteps.title: Electrolyse into propellant
buildSteps.detail: An electrolyser splits water into oxygen and hydrogen — about 0.89 kg of oxygen and 0.11 kg of hydrogen per kilogram of water. Both are liquefied and kept in cryogenic tanks, giving oxygen for breathing and oxygen-plus-hydrogen propellant for rockets.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Early units would produce kilograms of water a day for life support and small landers; propellant depots serving regular flights would need hundreds of tonnes a year, which means multiplying the number of excavators rather than making each one much bigger.

prerequisites.why: ice has been detected in polar cold traps and in impact ejecta, but its concentration, depth and physical form are still poorly known.

prerequisites.tech: Precision landing and driving in polar terrain
prerequisites.why: landers have reached the Moon, but the south pole is rough, shadowed and lit at a grazing angle, which defeats conventional landing cameras and solar power.

prerequisites.tech: Power that survives the lunar night
prerequisites.why: a mining plant cannot shut down for two weeks at a time; radioisotope power is proven at small scale and fission surface power is under development.

prerequisites.tech: Excavation and volatile capture in vacuum and deep cold
prerequisites.why: bench tests exist on Earth, but no machine has ever dug and processed regolith on another world.
keeping liquid oxygen and hydrogen for months without boiling off is a known problem with only partial solutions demonstrated in space.

pathway.milestone: remote sensing and landed prospecting — ice confirmed by lunar impact and orbital instruments, with rovers and payloads being sent to measure it directly
pathway.unlocks: a resource estimate good enough to design a plant around.

pathway.milestone: a robotic pilot that digs up regolith and captures water vapour on the Moon
pathway.unlocks: proof that the extraction step works outside a laboratory.

pathway.milestone: a pilot plant making water, oxygen and hydrogen at kilogram-per-day scale
pathway.unlocks: life support and refuelling for robotic and crewed landers, cutting the mass launched from Earth.

pathway.milestone: a polar propellant depot filling rockets from local ice
pathway.unlocks: routine travel between Earth and the Moon and onward to Mars without hauling propellant out of Earth's gravity well.

pathway.milestone: scaled extraction exporting water and propellant off the lunar surface
pathway.unlocks: a self-sustaining off-world supply chain — if the ice turns out to be concentrated enough to be worth mining.
